subject.title: [Feature]: Feishu Group Chat SubAgents for User-Specific Skills and Memory

question: Should Feishu group isolation stay within configurable sender/topic session routing and explicit thread-bound subagents, or should OpenClaw add automatic per-sender group subagent lifecycle with per-user skills, config, memory, admin controls, and cleanup?
rationale: The requested behavior spans Feishu channel routing, session state, per-agent config and skill authorization, memory isolation, quota/cost control, and lifecycle cleanup, which cannot be safely chosen by automation.

options.title: Constrain To Existing Seams
options.body: Keep groupSessionScope, bindings, and explicit thread-bound subagents as the supported path, then close or split this issue after documenting the recommended Feishu group pattern.

options.title: Design Plugin-Owned Automation
options.body: Approve a Feishu plugin-owned design for automatic per-sender group subagents with explicit storage, security, config-write, quota, and cleanup contracts before any implementation PR.

options.title: Split Into Narrow Issues
options.body: Break the request into smaller canonical issues for sender memory isolation, user skill preferences, threading-policy ergonomics, and lifecycle/admin controls.

recommendation.title: Constrain To Existing Seams
recommendation.body: Keep groupSessionScope, bindings, and explicit thread-bound subagents as the supported path, then close or split this issue after documenting the recommended Feishu group pattern.

likelyOwner.reason: The Feishu plugin is documented as community maintained by m1heng, and this is primarily a Feishu product/ownership decision.
